derivations.quote: Tensor this identity over the axes. Put $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$ (a permutation, not a ring), $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$. By the product rule the left sides combine to $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$, and the right sides to $\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ times $d$ factors $2^{2\alpha^2}$, so $RF_{\boldsymbol s}=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ with $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$ <cite data-source="paper">=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A,</cite>. Both $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B_0$ are contractions, applied one line at a time in a padded box of $T$ entries. Errors and times add over the $d$ passes: error below $dp^2$, time $O(dTp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ with a constant independent of $d$. Exposing each axis as the innermost field uses the [fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md), and with $t_i\in\{t_{\max}/2,t_{\max}\}$, $t_{\max}=2^\ell$, entries of $O(p)$ bits, exposing and restoring all lines costs $O(Tp\,d^2(1+\ell^\tau))$ <cite data-source="paper">then exposing and restoring all the lines costs</cite>. Since $t_i\ge t_{\max}/2$, at most $2dT/t_{\max}$ lines occur, so setup $O(p^g)$ per line ($g$ a fixed exponent) totals $O(dTp^g/t_{\max})=o(Tp)$ when $t_{\max}$ outgrows every power of $p$ and $d$ is polynomially bounded in $p$.
The source permutation $R$ cancels: $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+)[(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)]=u*v/S^2$.

relations.quote: Each prime-length transform is computed through a power-of-two one by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md)
The target permutation $Q$ is absorbed by the [Bluestein chirp identity](chirp.md)
